name: Malta
summary: Cannabis legal for adults since 2021 (limits; licensed non-profit associations). Up to 2 g of other drugs → Commissioner for Justice fine; more is criminal. Recreational nitrous oxide banned in 2026.
callingForHelp: No specific Good Samaritan law found. Health staff are bound by confidentiality; small-quantity possession is handled by the Commissioner for Justice rather than the courts.
drugChecking: No drug-checking service; harm-reduction groups have called for one.

lsd.note: Up to 2 g (gross) for own use: €75–125 fine from the Commissioner for Justice; a 2nd case within 2 years goes to a rehab board. More is a criminal offence.

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin is controlled. The 2 g small-quantity rule counts gross weight, so mushroom amounts can easily exceed it and become a criminal matter.

dmt.note: Up to 2 g (gross) for own use: €75–125 fine from the Commissioner for Justice; a 2nd case within 2 years goes to a rehab board. More is a criminal offence.

mescaline.note: Mescaline is controlled: up to 2 g for own use is a €75–125 fine (Commissioner for Justice); more is criminal. Status of cacti not confirmed.

dox.note: DOM, DOB, DOC are UN Schedule I: up to 2 g for own use is a €75–125 fine from the Commissioner for Justice; more is criminal.

nbomes.note: NBOMes are UN Schedule I: up to 2 g for own use is a €75–125 fine from the Commissioner for Justice; more is criminal.

2c-x.note: 2C-B is UN-controlled: up to 2 g for own use is a €75–125 fine from the Commissioner for Justice; more is criminal.

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T-2/2C-T-7 are not UN-scheduled; could not confirm whether Malta lists them.

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT and 5-MeO-MiPT are not UN-scheduled; could not confirm whether Malta lists them.

cannabis.note: 18+: up to 7 g in public, 50 g and 4 plants at home. 7–28 g: €50–100 fine; public use €235. Buy only via licensed non-profit associations.

ketamine.note: Prescription anaesthetic; could not confirm whether Malta schedules it as a controlled drug. If it does, the 2 g small-quantity fine rule applies.

mxe.note: UN Schedule II since 2016: up to 2 g for own use is a €75–125 fine from the Commissioner for Justice; more is criminal.

dxm.note: Not a controlled drug; could not confirm its pharmacy/prescription status in Malta.

nitrous.note: 2026 Public Health Act regulations ban importing, possessing, using or selling N2O for recreational purposes; legitimate uses exempt. Penalties unconfirmed.

amphetamines.note: Up to 2 g for own use: €75–125 fine (Commissioner for Justice); more is criminal. Prescription stimulants for ADHD are medical-only.

mdma.note: Up to 2 g (gross) for own use: €75–125 fine from the Commissioner for Justice; a 2nd case within 2 years goes to a rehab board. More is a criminal offence.

cocaine.note: Up to 2 g (gross) for own use: €75–125 fine from the Commissioner for Justice; a 2nd case within 2 years goes to a rehab board. More is a criminal offence.

caffeine.note: Not a controlled substance; sold freely.

alcohol.note: Legal; minimum age to buy alcohol is 17.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is UN Schedule II: up to 2 g (gross) for own use is a fine from the Commissioner for Justice. GBL/1,4-BD status not confirmed.

opioids.note: Heroin up to 2 g for own use: €75–125 fine (Commissioner for Justice); more is criminal. Prescription opioids are medical-only.

benzodiazepines.note: Prescription-only controlled psychotropics; small non-prescribed amounts fall under the Commissioner for Justice fine regime.

maois.note: MAOI antidepressants are prescription-only. Status of harmala alkaloids/ayahuasca not confirmed (DMT is controlled).
